label: F-01
title: The '067 floor' post-condition compares two numbers that are booked identically, so it cannot fail; story-067's zero-haircut anchor on the pre-migration booked total is not implemented
fingerprintProvenance: Copied verbatim from reports/31/script-audits/stable-staker-v2-cutover/classified-findings.json (not recomputed). finding-manager cross-check: sha256(fingerprintBasis) reproduces it byte-for-byte.
specConformance: standalone (story-082 Phase 6 post-conditions + story-067 zero-haircut floor)
description: Story 082 Phase 6 asks for "realized >= booked principal (067)", and story-067 defines that floor as realized principal versus the PRE-migration booked total (`principalOf(...) >= savedPreMigBookedDola`). The script instead asserts `strategy.principalOf(token, V2) >= V2.totalStaked` after migration. Both sides are credited with the same `credited` value in every `depositFor` (the strategy books `clientBalances[V2] += credited`, and V2 books `totalStaked += credited`), so the check holds with equality by construction and cannot detect a haircut. The executor's review carried this forward as a non-blocking Low, and the NatSpec, comment and revert string still call it the 067 floor. The real loss protection is the per-user bound, which was itself relaxed from the story's 0 bps + 2 wei to 2 bps + 2 wei (ERC4626) and 61 bps (USDe) by Decision 4. Same class as ledger YS-32 523ef3df52a6, where the story-067 floor measures the wrong quantity on migrate:ys-swap-cleanup.
impact: A reader or operator relies on a named safety gate that provides no protection. The aggregate pre-to-post principal change (USDe -8.934 USDe, USDC -0.170245, DOLA -0.00415) is never checked against any aggregate floor. Only per-user bps bounds apply, and they are looser than the story planned.
attackPath: N/A (assurance gap). Both sides of require(principalOf(V2) >= V2.totalStaked) are credited from the same `credited` value in depositFor, so equality holds by construction (fork: all three pools exactly equal).

classification.assetImpact: None directly. A named safety gate (the 'story-067 floor') is tautological, so no aggregate principal-loss gate exists; per-user bounds still stop a real vault loss.
attackPath: N/A (assurance gap). Both sides of require(principalOf(V2) >= V2.totalStaked) are credited from the same `credited` value in depositFor, so equality holds by construction (fork: all three pools exactly equal).

severityRationale: A Law-2 deviation: story-082 Phase 6 and story-067 define the floor against the PRE-migration booked total, and the implementation compares two lockstepped quantities. There is no asset impact because per-user bounds remain, so it is not H/M. It stays at Low rather than QA because it is the third recurrence of the story-067-floor defect class (YS-26 018c109ec76f, YS-32 523ef3df52a6) and misrepresents a safety gate to the operator.
recommendation: Replace it with a real aggregate gate anchored on the snapshot: require `V2.totalStaked_after >= P * (MAX_BPS - maxLossBps) / MAX_BPS - n * WEI_SLACK`, where P is `V1.migrationInfo(token).principalSnapshot`. Alternatively rename the check (for example 'V2 book/strategy lockstep') so it is not presented as the 067 floor, and record the Decision-4 relaxation as a human-accepted deviation.
evidence: Code (Core:469-471): `uint256 realized = ICutoverStrategy(strategy).principalOf(token, address(v2)); require(realized >= v2Staked, "cutover-post: strategy principal for V2 < V2 booked totalStaked (067 floor)");`. Fork @25975869 POSTPOOL (fork-logs/h-A-users-events.log): DOLA `v2Staked=1222723447469613917495|principalOfV2=1222723447469613917495`, USDC `1968305934|1968305934`, USDe `2557881617164101522200|2557881617164101522200`, all exactly equal. Story 067 text: `ysDolaV2.principalOf(DOLA, ORIGINAL_STABLE_STAKER) >= savedPreMigBookedDola`.

dedup.uniquenessVsSiblings: A tautology: both sides are booked from the same credited value. Distinct from SSV2C-01 (slack too tight), SSV2C-02 (preview self-heal) and SSV2C-05 (who bears the loss). SSV2C-05 cites the missing aggregate check only as context. Its fix (a top-up, or owner acceptance) does not repair the floor, and SSV2C-04's fix (a real aggregate floor) does not change the allocation.
